bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows the classic 1911 field strip as documented in Colt’s own Government-model manual, which Alchemy Custom Weaponry’s own page says the Alchemy Custom Weaponry Prime shares. It is not Alchemy Custom Weaponry’s manual for this model. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Alchemy Custom Weaponry exists for this model, but Alchemy Custom Weaponry’s own page says the Alchemy Custom Weaponry Prime is a 1911 of the classic, bushing-barrel kind, and that pattern’s take-down is documented by Colt’s own Government-model manual. This guide follows it. If what you see at the muzzle is not a separate bushing collar with a spring plug beneath it, stop at that step and clean the pistol locked open instead.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 9mm, .45 ACP. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Confirm yours is built the 1911 way
steps.action: Look before you touch: an external hammer, a thumb safety at the left rear, a grip safety in the backstrap, and at the muzzle a separate round collar — the barrel bushing — with a short spring plug beneath it. The bushing is the whole branch: this guide is written for the pistol that has one.
steps.prose: ⛔ No bushing, a bull barrel flush in the slide, or a full-length guide rod with a takedown hole? Stop here: that gun strips differently, and this guide would be wrong for it. Clean it locked open and put the question to Alchemy Custom Weaponry.

steps.title: Magazine out — catch it as it drops
steps.action: Hold your hand under the grip, press the magazine catch, and take the magazine as it comes free. Set it muzzle-side of the bench so it cannot find its way back in uninvited.
steps.quote: Place hand under magazine to prevent it from falling and press magazine catch to release and eject magazine.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 2, p.27

steps.title: Rack the chambered round out
steps.action: Using the slide’s serrations, pull the slide sharply rearward to extract and eject anything in the chamber. Let it run forward under control.
steps.quote: Using serrated finger grips pull slide sharply rearward to extract and eject a round from the chamber.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 3, p.27

steps.title: Look AND feel — and do it twice
steps.action: Draw the slide back and look into the chamber, then put a fingertip in: a case that hides from the eye cannot hide from a finger. Look down the empty magazine well too. Close under control, then check the same way a second time.
steps.quote: Pull slide back slightly and LOOK IN CHAMBER TO ENSURE
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — LOADING, step 3, p.24 (the look-in-chamber check, applied twice per the common floor)

steps.title: Proven empty, magazine out — now the strip begins
steps.action: The strip starts only on a pistol just proven empty with its magazine out. That is the book’s first instruction, and it is the one that keeps every later step boring.
steps.quote: Ensure magazine is removed and pistol is NOT loaded.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 1, p.34
steps.warn: ENSURE THAT MAGAZINE IS REMOVED AND THE PISTOL IS NOT LOADED BEFORE STRIPPING AND CLEANING, so that pistol will not fire

steps.title: Stand it on its butt, muzzle up
steps.action: Rest the pistol on the heel of its butt and the grip safety, muzzle pointing up. Everything at the muzzle end now works with gravity instead of against it.
steps.quote: With muzzle pointing upward, rest pistol on heel of butt and "grip safety" on a table or bench.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 2, p.35

steps.title: Free the plug: press down, turn the bushing
steps.action: Push the slide back about a quarter inch. Press the recoil spring plug down with your thumb and, holding it, rotate the barrel bushing clockwise about a quarter turn — a bushing wrench is the right tool if fingers will not move it, never pliers.
steps.quote: Push slide back about 1/4 inch, press down on recoil spring plug (located just below muzzle) and at same time rotate barrel bushing clockwise about 1/4 turn, using barrel bushing wrench if necessary; this will free plug and recoil
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 3 (A), p.35

steps.title: Let the plug and spring out under control
steps.action: Keep your thumb over the plug — it is under real spring pressure and will fly if it slips — and let the plug and spring extend slowly out of the slide. Lift them clear.
steps.quote: Keep pressure on plug to prevent it being ejected by the spring, then allow plug and spring to gradually extend out of the slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 3 (A), p.35

steps.title: Cock the hammer
steps.action: Pull the hammer back by its spur until it cocks. The slide cannot come off over a lowered hammer.
steps.quote: Cock hammer by pulling back on hammer spur.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 4, p.36

steps.title: Line up the disassembly notch
steps.action: Draw the slide back slowly until the small half-moon notch in its left edge sits opposite the rear lug of the slide stop, and hold it there. The notch is the only place the slide stop comes out; forced anywhere else it scratches the long arc into the frame every 1911 owner learns to dread.
steps.quote: Pull slide to rear until lug on slide stop is opposite disassembly notch
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 5, p.36

steps.title: Slide stop out to the left
steps.action: Push the slide stop’s pin from the right side of the frame and lift the slide stop out of the left.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 6, p.37

steps.title: Slide forward off the receiver
steps.action: Hold the receiver and run the slide forward off the front of the rails. Set the receiver down — the hammer, sear and grip safety inside it stay untouched.
steps.quote: Push slide forward off the receiver.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 7, p.37

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out the back of the slide
steps.action: Turn the slide over, lift the recoil spring and its guide, and draw them rearward out of the slide. Note which way the guide’s collar faced.
steps.quote: Lift recoil springs and guide and pull them rearward out of slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 8 (A & B), p.37

steps.title: Bushing off, barrel out the front — and that is the limit
steps.action: Turn the bushing the other way and lift it off the muzzle, then tip the barrel’s link forward and draw the barrel out of the front of the slide. That is the whole field strip, and the book draws the line in its own words below. The firing pin and its stop, the extractor, the mainspring housing: Alchemy Custom Weaponry’s work, not bench work.
steps.quote: Push link forward and remove barrel from slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — MK IV/Series 80 and 90 Pistols — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, steps 9 and 10, p.37
steps.warn: Do not strip your pistol further than previously described. Do not remove or alter parts, particularly safety parts.

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, rails and ramp wiped
steps.action: Brush the bore wet with solvent from the chamber end, then dry patches until clean and a lightly oiled patch for storage. Wipe the breech face, both sets of rails and the feed ramp with a cloth and a little solvent; a thin film of oil on the rails, the barrel where it rubs, the locking lugs and the link. No oil into the firing-pin hole, and a dry patch through the bore before you shoot.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the slide, the receiver and the barrel for cracks, the recoil spring for kinks or a broken coil, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Alchemy Custom Weaponry.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Alchemy Custom Weaponry has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Alchemy Custom Weaponry Prime, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Alchemy Custom Weaponry exists for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Alchemy Custom Weaponry, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush wet with bore solvent, from the chamber end
Dry patches until clean, then a lightly oiled patch for storage
A dry patch through before the next shot

cleaning.name: BREECH, RAILS & FEED RAMP
tasks: Breech face wiped, carbon off with a nylon brush
Feed ramp and barrel throat wiped smooth
⛔ No solvent or oil into the firing-pin hole

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A thin film on the rails
A drop on the barrel where it rubs, the locking lugs and the link

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Barrel into the slide, link forward
reassembly.action: Slide upside down, barrel link tipped forward, and the barrel in through the front.
reassembly.quote: (A & B) With slide upside down and barrel link forward, assemble barrel into the slide, as in Figure 10.

reassembly.title: Bushing over the muzzle and turned home
reassembly.action: Bushing over the muzzle, into the slide until flush with the slide’s face, then turned clockwise as far as it goes.
reassembly.quote: Place barrel bushing over muzzle of barrel and into slide until it is flush with the face of the slide, (STEP 1). Turn bushing clockwise as far as it will go, (Step 2).

reassembly.title: Guide into the spring, closed end to the collar
reassembly.action: The recoil spring guide goes into the spring so the spring’s closed end sits against the guide’s collar, and the pair into the slide from the rear, arched collar riding the barrel.
reassembly.quote: Place the recoil guide into the recoil spring/s so that the closed end of

reassembly.title: Hammer cocked, plunger lever down, slide onto the receiver
reassembly.action: Cock the hammer, confirm the plunger lever on top of the receiver sits down and forward, tip the receiver forward to keep it there, and run the slide onto the rails from the front.
reassembly.quote: Cock the hammer. Look at the top of the receiver and make sure the plunger lever is down (forward), tip the receiver forward to keep it down as you run the slide onto the receiver

reassembly.title: Slide stop in through the link — never hammered
reassembly.action: Move the slide until the hole in the barrel link lines up with the frame’s hole, insert the slide stop until it is almost home, draw the slide to the disassembly notch, and press the slide stop up and in until it seats. If it will not go with fingers, the link is not lined up — lift the barrel’s rear a little through the magazine well and try again.
reassembly.quote: Insert the slide stop through the hole until it is almost home

reassembly.title: Plug compressed, bushing locked over it
reassembly.action: Muzzle up on the bench: push the slide back a quarter inch, press the plug down over the spring until it is home, and rotate the bushing so its arch straddles and locks the plug.
reassembly.quote: Push slide back about 1/4 inch, press down on recoil spring plug, compressing the recoil spring into the slide until the plug is fully home, then rotate the barrel bushing.

fncheck: Magazine out, chamber proven empty twice. Pull the slide fully back and release: it should fly forward and close with the hammer staying cocked. Push the thumb safety up — it should move cleanly and hold — and with it down, confirm the grip safety springs back out when released. Rack the slide several times with an empty magazine in: smooth travel, and lock-open on the last stroke. This check never asks you to press the trigger; Colt’s own book warns never to dry fire with the slide off, and whether this pistol tolerates dry firing assembled is a question for Alchemy Custom Weaponry.
